skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================

8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("pde.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("pde.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::{
15.     mem::paging::TableEntry,
16.     x86::mem::paging::{
17.         flags::{
18.             AccessedFlag,
19.             DirtyFlag,
20.             PageCacheDisableFlag,
21.             PageSizeFlag,
22.             PageWriteThroughFlag,
23.             PresentFlag,
24.             ReadWriteFlag,
25.             UserSupervisorFlag,
26.         },
27.         frame::FrameNumber,
28.         PteWord,
29.     },
30. };
31. 
32. //==================================================================================================
33. // Page Directory Entry Flags
34. //==================================================================================================
35. 
36. ///
37. /// # Description
38. ///
39. /// A type that represents flags of a page directory entry.
40. ///
41. #[verus_verify]
42. #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
43. pub struct PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
44.     /// Present flag.
45.     present: PresentFlag,
46.     /// Read/write flag.
47.     read_write: ReadWriteFlag,
48.     /// User/supervisor flag.
49.     user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag,
50.     /// Page write-through flag.
51.     page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag,
52.     /// Page cache disable flag.
53.     page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag,
54.     /// Accessed flag.
55.     accessed: AccessedFlag,
56.     /// Dirty flag.
57.     dirty: DirtyFlag,
58.     /// Page size flag (PDE-only, bit 7).
59.     page_size: PageSizeFlag,
60. }
61. 
62. #[verus_verify]
63. impl PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
64.     ///
65.     /// # Description
66.     ///
67.     /// Constructs a [`PageDirectoryEntryFlags`] with the given flags.
68.     ///
69.     /// # Parameters
70.     ///
71.     /// - `present`: The present flag.
72.     /// - `read_write`: The read/write flag.
73.     /// - `user_supervisor`: The user/supervisor flag.
74.     /// - `page_write_through`: The page write-through flag.
75.     /// - `page_cache_disable`: The page cache disable flag.
76.     /// - `accessed`: The accessed flag.
77.     /// - `dirty`: The dirty flag.
78.     /// - `page_size`: The page size flag.
79.     ///
80.     /// # Returns
81.     ///
82.     /// A [`PageDirectoryEntryFlags`].
83.     ///
84.     #[verus_spec(result =>
85.         ensures
86.             result@ == spec_pde_flags_new(
87.                 present,
88.                 read_write,
89.                 user_supervisor,
90.                 page_write_through,
91.                 page_cache_disable,
92.                 accessed,
93.                 dirty,
94.                 page_size,
95.             ),
96.     )]
97.     pub fn new(
98.         present: PresentFlag,
99.         read_write: ReadWriteFlag,
100.         user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag,
101.         page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag,
102.         page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag,
103.         accessed: AccessedFlag,
104.         dirty: DirtyFlag,
105.         page_size: PageSizeFlag,
106.     ) -> Self {
107.         Self {
108.             present,
109.             read_write,
110.             user_supervisor,
111.             page_write_through,
112.             page_cache_disable,
113.             accessed,
114.             dirty,
115.             page_size,
116.         }
117.     }
118. }
119. 
120. impl PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
121.     ///
122.     /// # Description
123.     ///
124.     /// Checks if the present flag is set.
125.     ///
126.     /// # Returns
127.     ///
128.     /// `true` if the present flag is set, `false` otherwise.
129.     ///
130.     #[inline(always)]
131.     #[verus_spec(result =>
132.         ensures result == self@.present,
133.     )]
134.     pub fn is_present(&self) -> bool {
135.         matches!(self.present, PresentFlag::Present)
136.     }
137. 
138.     ///
139.     /// # Description
140.     ///
141.     /// Checks if the user flag is set (i.e., user-mode access is allowed).
142.     ///
143.     /// # Returns
144.     ///
145.     /// `true` if the user flag is set, `false` otherwise.
146.     ///
147.     #[inline(always)]
148.     pub fn is_user(&self) -> bool {
149.         matches!(self.user_supervisor, UserSupervisorFlag::User)
150.     }
151. 
152.     ///
153.     /// # Description
154.     ///
155.     /// Checks if the read/write flag is set (i.e., the page is writable).
156.     ///
157.     /// # Returns
158.     ///
159.     /// `true` if the page is writable, `false` otherwise.
160.     ///
161.     #[inline(always)]
162.     pub fn is_writable(&self) -> bool {
163.         matches!(self.read_write, ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite)
164.     }
165. 
166.     ///
167.     /// # Description
168.     ///
169.     /// Sets read/write flag.
170.     ///
171.     /// # Parameters
172.     ///
173.     /// - `read_write`: The read/write flag.
174.     ///
175.     #[inline(always)]
176.     pub fn set_read_write(&mut self, read_write: ReadWriteFlag) {
177.         self.read_write = read_write;
178.     }
179. 
180.     ///
181.     /// # Description
182.     ///
183.     /// Sets user/supervisor flag.
184.     ///
185.     /// # Parameters
186.     ///
187.     /// - `user_supervisor`: The user/supervisor flag.
188.     ///
189.     #[inline(always)]
190.     pub fn set_user_supervisor(&mut self, user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag) {
191.         self.user_supervisor = user_supervisor;
192.     }
193. 
194.     ///
195.     /// # Description
196.     ///
197.     /// Checks if the page size flag is set (large page).
198.     ///
199.     /// # Returns
200.     ///
201.     /// `true` if the page size flag is set, `false` otherwise.
202.     ///
203.     #[inline(always)]
204.     pub fn is_large_page(&self) -> bool {
205.         matches!(self.page_size, PageSizeFlag::Large)
206.     }
207. 
208.     ///
209.     /// # Description
210.     ///
211.     /// Sets page size.
212.     ///
213.     /// # Parameters
214.     ///
215.     /// - `page_size`: The page size flag.
216.     ///
217.     #[inline(always)]
218.     pub fn set_page_size(&mut self, page_size: PageSizeFlag) {
219.         self.page_size = page_size;
220.     }
221. 
222.     ///
223.     /// # Description
224.     ///
225.     /// Constructs a [`PageDirectoryEntryFlags`] from a raw value.
226.     ///
227.     /// # Parameters
228.     ///
229.     /// - `value`: The raw value.
230.     ///
231.     /// # Returns
232.     ///
233.     /// A [`PageDirectoryEntryFlags`].
234.     ///
235.     fn from_raw_value(value: PteWord) -> Self {
236.         Self {
237.             present: PresentFlag::from_raw_value(value),
238.             read_write: ReadWriteFlag::from_raw_value(value),
239.             user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag::from_raw_value(value),
240.             page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag::from_raw_value(value),
241.             page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag::from_raw_value(value),
242.             accessed: AccessedFlag::from_raw_value(value),
243.             dirty: DirtyFlag::from_raw_value(value),
244.             page_size: PageSizeFlag::from_raw_value(value),
245.         }
246.     }
247. 
248.     ///
249.     /// # Description
250.     ///
251.     /// Converts a [`PageDirectoryEntryFlags`] into a raw value.
252.     ///
253.     /// # Returns
254.     ///
255.     /// The raw value.
256.     ///
257.     fn into_raw_value(self) -> PteWord {
258.         let mut value: PteWord = 0;
259. 
260.         value |= self.present.into_raw_value();
261.         value |= self.read_write.into_raw_value();
262.         value |= self.user_supervisor.into_raw_value();
263.         value |= self.page_write_through.into_raw_value();
264.         value |= self.page_cache_disable.into_raw_value();
265.         value |= self.accessed.into_raw_value();
266.         value |= self.dirty.into_raw_value();
267.         value |= self.page_size.into_raw_value();
268. 
269.         value
270.     }
271. }
272. 
273. //==================================================================================================
274. // Page Directory Entry
275. //==================================================================================================
276. 
277. ///
278. /// # Description
279. ///
280. /// A type that represents a page directory entry.
281. ///
282. #[verus_verify]
283. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
284. pub struct PageDirectoryEntry {
285.     /// Flags.
286.     flags: PageDirectoryEntryFlags,
287.     /// Physical address of the page table (or large page).
288.     frame: FrameNumber,
289. }
290. 
291. impl PageDirectoryEntry {
292.     /// Size in bytes of the hardware page directory entry representation (32-bit encoded value).
293.     pub const SIZE: usize = ::core::mem::size_of::<PteWord>();
294. }
295. 
296. #[verus_verify]
297. impl PageDirectoryEntry {
298.     ///
299.     /// # Description
300.     ///
301.     /// Constructs a [`PageDirectoryEntry`] with the given flags and frame number.
302.     ///
303.     /// # Parameters
304.     ///
305.     /// - `flags`: The flags.
306.     /// - `frame`: The frame number.
307.     ///
308.     /// # Returns
309.     ///
310.     /// A [`PageDirectoryEntry`].
311.     ///
312.     #[verus_spec(result =>
313.         ensures
314.             result@ == spec_pde_new(flags@, frame@),
315.             result.inv(),
316.     )]
317.     pub fn new(flags: PageDirectoryEntryFlags, frame: FrameNumber) -> Self {
318.         proof! { use_type_invariant(frame); }
319.         Self { flags, frame }
320.     }
321. }
322. 
323. impl PageDirectoryEntry {
324.     ///
325.     /// # Description
326.     ///
327.     /// Constructs a [`PageDirectoryEntry`] from a raw 32-bit value.
328.     ///
329.     /// # Parameters
330.     ///
331.     /// - `value`: The raw value.
332.     ///
333.     /// # Returns
334.     ///
335.     /// - `Some(`[`PageDirectoryEntry`]`)`: If the raw value is valid.
336.     /// - `None`: Otherwise.
337.     ///
338.     pub fn from_raw_value(value: PteWord) -> Option<Self> {
339.         Some(Self {
340.             flags: PageDirectoryEntryFlags::from_raw_value(value),
341.             frame: FrameNumber::from_raw_value(value as usize >> crate::mem::FRAME_SHIFT)?,
342.         })
343.     }
344. 
345.     ///
346.     /// # Description
347.     ///
348.     /// Converts a [`PageDirectoryEntry`] into a raw 32-bit value.
349.     ///
350.     /// # Returns
351.     ///
352.     /// The raw value.
353.     ///
354.     pub fn into_raw_value(self) -> PteWord {
355.         let mut value: PteWord = 0;
356. 
357.         value |= self.flags.into_raw_value();
358.         value |= (self.frame.into_raw_value() << crate::mem::FRAME_SHIFT) as PteWord;
359. 
360.         value
361.     }
362. 
363.     ///
364.     /// # Description
365.     ///
366.     /// Returns the flags associated with the target page directory entry.
367.     ///
368.     /// # Returns
369.     ///
370.     /// The flags.
371.     ///
372.     pub fn flags(&self) -> PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
373.         self.flags
374.     }
375. 
376.     ///
377.     /// # Description
378.     ///
379.     /// Checks if the target page directory entry is marked as present.
380.     ///
381.     /// # Returns
382.     ///
383.     /// `true`: If the target page directory entry is marked as present.
384.     /// `false`: Otherwise.
385.     ///
386.     #[verus_spec(result =>
387.         ensures result == self@.flags.present,
388.     )]
389.     pub fn is_present(&self) -> bool {
390.         self.flags.is_present()
391.     }
392. 
393.     ///
394.     /// # Description
395.     ///
396.     /// Returns the frame number of the target page directory entry.
397.     ///
398.     /// # Returns
399.     ///
400.     /// The frame number.
401.     ///
402.     pub fn frame_number(&self) -> FrameNumber {
403.         self.frame
404.     }
405. 
406.     ///
407.     /// # Description
408.     ///
409.     /// Returns the physical address (frame number × frame size) of the page frame.
410.     ///
411.     /// # Returns
412.     ///
413.     /// The physical address.
414.     ///
415.     #[verus_spec(result =>
416.         ensures
417.             result as int == self@.frame * (crate::mem::FRAME_SIZE as int),
418.             result as int % (crate::mem::FRAME_SIZE as int) == 0,
419.     )]
420.     // VERUS REWRITE: the original `self.frame.into_raw_value() << crate::mem::FRAME_SHIFT`
421.     // (single expression) is split so the `into_raw_value()` postcondition
422.     // (`0 <= self@ <= FrameNumber::spec_max()`) lands in context *before* the overflow-bearing
423.     // shift, and `lemma_frame_address(raw)` can be invoked between them to discharge the
424.     // no-overflow + `FRAME_SIZE`-alignment `ensures`. The operand must be named (`let raw`)
425.     // because an exec call cannot appear inside `proof!`, so there is otherwise no point between
426.     // the call and the shift to invoke the lemma. Same value, same operations, same time/space
427.     // complexity — semantically equivalent.
428.     // Reproducer: verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-arch-x86-pde/cheating-elimination/repro/frame_address.rs
429.     pub fn frame_address(&self) -> usize {
430.         let raw: usize = self.frame.into_raw_value();
431.         proof! { lemma_frame_address(raw); }
432.         raw << crate::mem::FRAME_SHIFT
433.     }
434. 
435.     ///
436.     /// # Description
437.     ///
438.     /// Checks if the page size flag is set.
439.     ///
440.     /// # Returns
441.     ///
442.     /// `true` if the page size flag is set, `false` otherwise.
443.     ///
444.     pub fn is_large_page(&self) -> bool {
445.         self.flags.is_large_page()
446.     }
447. 
448.     ///
449.     /// # Description
450.     ///
451.     /// Sets page size.
452.     ///
453.     /// # Parameters
454.     ///
455.     /// - `page_size`: The page size flag.
456.     ///
457.     pub fn set_page_size(&mut self, page_size: PageSizeFlag) {
458.         self.flags.set_page_size(page_size);
459.     }
460. 
461.     ///
462.     /// # Description
463.     ///
464.     /// Sets read/write flag in the target page directory entry.
465.     ///
466.     /// # Parameters
467.     ///
468.     /// - `read_write`: The read/write flag.
469.     ///
470.     pub fn set_read_write(&mut self, read_write: ReadWriteFlag) {
471.         self.flags.set_read_write(read_write);
472.     }
473. 
474.     ///

2. name: proof-extraction
3. description: "Extract large inline proof blocks from exec code into named lemmas in .proof.rs. Use when polishing verified code to improve readability and proof organization."
4. ---
5. 
6. # Proof Extraction
7. 
8. Extract large inline `proof { ... }` blocks from exec code into named lemmas
9. in the proof file (`<module>.proof.rs`).
10. 
11. ## Why
12. 
13. Large inline proof blocks hurt readability and make exec code hard to review.
14. Extracting them into lemmas with clear names documents *what* is being proven
15. and makes proofs reusable.
16. 
17. ## Tool
18. 
19. Use `check_proof_blocks` (MCP tool) or the CLI script to find blocks:
20. 
21. ```bash
22. python3 scripts/check_proof_blocks.py <source_file> --threshold 5 --all
23. ```
24. 
25. Output shows each proof block with its enclosing function, line range, and size.
26. Blocks marked `⚠️ EXTRACT` exceed the threshold.
27. 
28. ## Rules
29. 
30. | Block size  | Action |
31. |-------------|--------|
32. | >5 lines    | **Must** extract into a lemma in `.proof.rs` |
33. | 4-5 lines   | Extract if generic/reusable; keep if tightly coupled to exec context |
34. | 1-3 lines   | Keep inline |
35. 
36. ## Extraction Process
37. 
38. For each block to extract:
39. 
40. 1. Read the proof block and identify what it proves (the key `assert` / property).
41. 2. Create `proof fn lemma_<descriptive_name>` in `.proof.rs` with:
42.    - `requires`: the preconditions the proof depends on
43.    - `ensures`: the property being proven (must be strong enough for the call site)
44. 3. Replace the inline block with a 1-3 line lemma call.
45. 4. Run verification to confirm it still passes.
46. 
47. ## Loop Invariants
48. 
49. Long loop invariants (>5 clauses) also hurt readability. Factor out groups
50. of related clauses into named `spec fn` predicates:
51. 
52. ```rust
53. // Before: 10 invariant clauses inline
54. while i < n
55.     invariant
56.         0 <= i <= n,
57.         result.len() == i,
58.         forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j]),
59.         ... // 7 more clauses
60. { ... }
61. 
62. // After: grouped into named predicates
63. spec fn loop_partial_result_ok(result: Seq<T>, input: Seq<T>, i: int) -> bool {
64.     result.len() == i
65.     && forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j])
66. }
67. 
68. while i < n
69.     invariant
70.         0 <= i <= n,
71.         loop_partial_result_ok(result@, input@, i as int),
72.         ... // remaining clauses
73. { ... }
74. ```
75. 
76. Keep trivial bounds (`0 <= i <= n`) inline. Extract semantic groups
77. (data consistency, structural invariants) into named predicates.
78. 
79. ## Naming
80. 
81. Lemma names describe what they prove:
82. - ✅ `lemma_set_bit_preserves_inv`
83. - ✅ `lemma_alloc_range_bounded`
84. - ❌ `lemma_proof_block_1`
85. - ❌ `lemma_helper`
86. 
87. ## Constraints
88. 
89. - Do NOT change exec logic.
90. - Do NOT change spec function signatures.
91. - Verification must still pass after extraction.
92.

 # Proof Extraction
 
 Extract large inline `proof { ... }` blocks from exec code into named lemmas
 in the proof file (`<module>.proof.rs`).
 
 ## Why
 
 Large inline proof blocks hurt readability and make exec code hard to review.
 Extracting them into lemmas with clear names documents *what* is being proven
 and makes proofs reusable.
 
 ## Tool
 
 Use `check_proof_blocks` (MCP tool) or the CLI script to find blocks:

 ```
 
 Output shows each proof block with its enclosing function, line range, and size.
 Blocks marked `⚠️ EXTRACT` exceed the threshold.
 
 ## Rules
 
 | Block size  | Action |
 |-------------|--------|
 | >5 lines    | **Must** extract into a lemma in `.proof.rs` |
 | 4-5 lines   | Extract if generic/reusable; keep if tightly coupled to exec context |
 | 1-3 lines   | Keep inline |
 
 ## Extraction Process
 
 For each block to extract:
 
 1. Read the proof block and identify what it proves (the key `assert` / property).
 2. Create `proof fn lemma_<descriptive_name>` in `.proof.rs` with:
    - `requires`: the preconditions the proof depends on
    - `ensures`: the property being proven (must be strong enough for the call site)
 3. Replace the inline block with a 1-3 line lemma call.
 4. Run verification to confirm it still passes.

 Long loop invariants (>5 clauses) also hurt readability. Factor out groups
 of related clauses into named `spec fn` predicates:

 // Before: 10 invariant clauses inline
 while i < n
     invariant
         0 <= i <= n,
         result.len() == i,
         forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j]),
         ... // 7 more clauses
 { ... }

 spec fn loop_partial_result_ok(result: Seq<T>, input: Seq<T>, i: int) -> bool {
     result.len() == i
     && forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j])
 }
 
 while i < n
     invariant
         0 <= i <= n,
         loop_partial_result_ok(result@, input@, i as int),
         ... // remaining clauses
 { ... }
 ```
 
 Keep trivial bounds (`0 <= i <= n`) inline. Extract semantic groups
 (data consistency, structural invariants) into named predicates.

 Lemma names describe what they prove:
 - ✅ `lemma_set_bit_preserves_inv`
 - ✅ `lemma_alloc_range_bounded`
 - ❌ `lemma_proof_block_1`
 - ❌ `lemma_helper`

 - Do NOT change exec logic.
 - Do NOT change spec function signatures.

1. ---
2. name: proof-minimization
3. description: "Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity."
4. ---
5. 
6. # Proof Minimization
7. 
8. Remove redundant proof artifacts to make verification lean and readable
9. without weakening any guarantees.
10. 
11. ## What to Remove
12. 
13. 1. **Redundant lemmas** — another lemma proves the exact same property
14.    (same `requires` AND same `ensures`).
15. 2. **Redundant assertions** — `assert` statements that Verus can verify
16.    without them. Remove in bulk, then re-run verification.
17. 3. **Redundant proof hints** — unnecessary `by`, `by(nonlinear_arith)`,
18.    or trigger annotations that Verus doesn't need.
19. 4. **Dead spec functions** — non-public spec functions with zero callers (not
20.    referenced in any `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, or lemma). Keep
21.    `pub` spec functions — they may be part of the module's API for dependents.
22. 5. **Debug artifacts** — In spec/proof files: remove TODO comments, commented-out
23.    code, and property-ID annotations (e.g., `// FUNC-POST-3`, `// INV-2`). In
24.    exec files: remove unnecessary verification-related comments (e.g., obsolete
25.    proof hints, property-ID tags); do NOT remove original source comments.
26. 
27. ## What is NOT Redundant
28. 
29. - **Uncalled lemmas**: Verus verifies all lemmas regardless of callers.
30.   An uncalled lemma still proves a property. Only remove if another lemma
31.   proves the *exact* same thing.
32. - **Different preconditions**: Two lemmas with different `requires` prove
33.   different properties even if `ensures` looks similar.
34. 
35. **When in doubt, keep it.**
36. 
37. ## Process
38. 
39. This is a best-effort pass for readability, not an exhaustive search.
40. 
41. 1. **Assertions**: Remove `assert` statements that look redundant based on context.
42. 2. **Lemmas**: Remove a lemma only if another has identical `requires` + `ensures`.
43. 3. **Proof hints**: Remove `by(...)` annotations that look unnecessary.
44. 4. Re-run verification after changes — if it fails, revert the removal.
45. 
46. ## Constraints
47. 
48. - Do NOT add `assume`, `admit`, or `external_body`.
49. - Do NOT weaken any `ensures` or remove any meaningful property.
50. - Verification must pass after every removal batch.
51.
